title: His own Apollo recordings with Charlie Parker in 1944
summary: For Apollo around 1944 he led sessions with Charlie Parker, Dexter Gordon, Buck Clayton, J. C. Heard, Jimmy Butts and others, playing mostly his originals.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Playing with and understanding Thelonious Monk

blocks.x: Right. Well, had you -- I mean, how much recording had you done by then?

Well, by that time then I had already -- I more or less had established myself in the recording field of jazz, with some recordings that I'd done previous to all of these things with Apollo Records. I made my first recordings on my own, with Apollo Record Company. I think this was about 1944, and I made some great arrangements and some great tunes, and recordings, and I had in the band a great personnel with Charlie Parker as one of my side men. Charlie Parker was on alto saxophone, and Dexter Gordon was on tenor saxophone, and Buck Clayton, my old friend and mentor was willing to help me out and he played the trumpet. And I had such great musicians as J. C. Heard on the drums and on some of those recordings I made later I had Osie O.-C. Johnson --

And of course as I said these records that I'm talking about now in '44 had -- I had a bass player by the name of Jimmy Butts who was a New York bass player, and I had a guitarist who was with Cab Calloway. And I had a real fine group there. I made some great tunes and --
Many of them were originals, weren't they?
Most of them were originals, most of
all of them were originals. Out of that came a song called "Tune Us In," and Sir Charles -- let's see, "20th Century Blues," and "Street Beat," and -- oh, I can't think of all of them but--
